title: Inferring behind-the-meter demand components from net load via inverse optimization
abstract: arXiv:2410.02774v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Understanding and forecasting electricity demand responses to price signals is essential to support the operational decisions of system operators, retailers, and regulators. Traditional time series and machine learning approaches have performed well under stable consumption patterns. However, the rise of active consumers with flexible assets, such as solar-plus-storage systems and electric vehicles, introduces new complexities. These consumers exhibit behind-the-meter behavior that is generally unobservable to system operators and retailers, who can typically only measure net demand at the boundary meters which are located at the connection points to the grid. Net demand reflects the aggregate of baseload consumption, flexible load shifting, and self-generation, all of which may respond nonlinearly to market prices. translated_title: 通过逆向优化从净负荷中推断表后需求成分
translated_abstract: 了解和预测电力需求对价格信号的响应，对于支持系统运营商、零售商和监管机构的运营决策至关重要。传统的时间序列和机器学习方法在稳定的消费模式下表现良好。然而，拥有柔性资产（如光伏加储能系统和电动汽车）的主动消费者的兴起带来了新的复杂性。这些消费者表现出通常对系统运营商和零售商不可观察的“表后”行为，而运营商和零售商通常只能测量位于电网连接点处的边界电表所记录的净需求。净需求反映了基础负荷消费、柔性负荷转移和自发电的总和，所有这些成分都可能对市场价格做出非线性响应。随着这些不可观察成分的不断增长，现有的预测模型可能无法捕捉电力消费的真实动态。
tldr: 本文提出一种基于逆向优化的方法，从可观测的净负荷数据中反推表后需求成分（基础负荷、柔性负荷转移和自发电），以更好地理解和预测主动消费者对价格信号的响应。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an inverse optimization approach to infer behind-the-meter demand components (baseload, flexible load shifting, and self-generation) from observable net load data, enabling better understanding and forecasting of active consumers' responses to price signals.
